title: Biryani, Pav Bhaji, and 6,200 Orders a Minute: What India Ate While Watching IPL 2026
excerpt: Swiggy's data from the just-concluded IPL season reveals a 32% surge in food orders, a ₹2.14-lakh restaurant bill in Bengaluru, and biryani's undisputed reign as cricket's comfort food.
body:
Cricket and food have always been inseparable in India. But the numbers from IPL 2026 — the season that ended with Royal Challengers Bengaluru lifting their second consecutive title — reveal just how deeply the two are intertwined.

## The Numbers Don't Lie

Swiggy's IPL 2026 Food Ordering and Dining Insights report paints a picture of a nation that eats as passionately as it cheers. The headline figure: a 32.31% increase in food delivery orders compared to IPL 2025, with metro cities like Bengaluru, Mumbai, and Hyderabad leading the charge.

During the final on May 31, when RCB defeated Gujarat Titans to seal their back-to-back championship, Swiggy recorded an average of 1,300 orders per minute. At the peak — 7:56 PM, roughly the moment when Virat Kohli was in the middle of his match-winning 75 not out — that number spiked to over 6,200 orders per minute.

## India's IPL Menu

What did 300 million cricket fans eat? The answers are both predictable and delightful.

**Main courses:** Chicken Biryani topped the charts once again, followed by Chicken Fried Rice and — somewhat surprisingly — Veg Burgers. Biryani's dominance during cricket season has become so reliable that it practically functions as an economic indicator.

**Snacks:** Pav Bhaji and Chicken Popcorn emerged as the most popular nibbles during the final matches — proof that India's cricket snacking habits straddle the traditional and the modern.

**Desserts:** The sweet tooth was out in full force during the qualifier and final matches. Choco lava cakes, tender coconut ice cream, and ras malai were the most-ordered desserts, a delicious cross-section of India's diverse palate.

## Dining Out for Cricket

It wasn't just delivery. Swiggy's Dineout platform reported a 41% jump in restaurant bookings compared to IPL 2025, with Bengaluru, Delhi, Hyderabad, Mumbai, and Pune recording the highest reservations.

The cricket fever was equally strong in Tier-II cities, with Ahmedabad, Jaipur, Chandigarh, and Lucknow seeing significant restaurant traffic on match days.

One group of 20 diners in Bengaluru celebrated with a Swiggy Dineout bill of ₹2,14,061 — roughly $2,500 — while watching the match on May 29. That's one way to toast a championship run.

## The Diaspora Connection

For NRIs watching IPL from living rooms in New Jersey, Houston, and the Bay Area, the food ritual takes a different but equally passionate form. Group WhatsApp chats buzz with biryani orders from local Indian restaurants. Watch parties at desi eateries sell out. And in a poignant echo of the Swiggy data, biryani and chai remain the go-to orders for diaspora cricket nights too.

The IPL has become one of the few cultural events that synchronises eating habits across the Indian world — from Bengaluru to Birmingham, from Hyderabad to Houston.

## What's Next

As IPL continues to grow into one of the world's most-watched sporting events, the food industry is increasingly designing around it. Expect more IPL-themed menus, cricket night promotions at Indian restaurants in the US, and an ever-deepening fusion of fandom and flavour.

In the meantime, one thing is clear: as long as there is cricket, there will be biryani.

*Sources: Curly Tales, Swiggy IPL 2026 Food Ordering and Dining Insights*
author: Diaspora Desk
